label: D2 a1->S1 common: grows with episode time, a1-leaning policy logit, last reward
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * np.minimum(ep_trial, 80) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * np.maximum(choice, 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * (prev_reward==1)
explanation: Silent at D1 and GO; fires only at D2 after the agent chose a1 and commonly reached S1 (a1/S2, a2/S1, a2/S2 are all ~0). Within a1->S1 D2 steps, magnitude rises roughly linearly with trial in episode (near 0 early, ~1.3-1.5 late), with the model positive (a1-favouring) policy logit at that D2 step (ReLU of choice), and is higher when the previous trial was rewarded. Previous-trial pattern adds little once choice is included (a1 S2 u looks strong in the raw table, but that is mostly the a1 preference). Without the model logit, history-only terms (prev reward, last two actions) reach only ~0.34 dev. Underpredicts the largest late-episode activations (linear terms cannot capture the saturation). Test R2 beyond timing 0.56 (dev 0.58), above the additive all ceiling 0.42.

issues: The claim that it 'grows with last reward' has the wrong sign when taken alone. With base + time + B*(prev_reward==1) the reward weight is -0.139 (test R^2 0.232). Activation is higher after an unrewarded previous trial: in the worst-fit windows a1->S1 D2 steps after r0 reach about 1.5, and after r1 they are about 1.3 falling to 0.6-0.9. The +0.199 weight in the claimed fit appears only once max(choice,0) is in the model, so it is a conditional correction, not a driver. The label states it as a raw positive effect.

The explanation calls the previous-trial pattern 'little', but the a1 S2 u residual at D2 is +0.327, the largest history cell. History-only terms scaled by time reach test 0.39, a bit above the 0.34 quoted.

The additive form misses a strong multiplicative interaction. Adding B*max(choice,0)*min(ep_trial,80) raises test R^2 from 0.557 to 0.675. Gating that product by prev_reward==1 raises it to 0.744 on test and 0.762 on dev. So the a1-logit effect grows with episode time; it does not just add to it. That is the main source of the 'underpredicts largest late activations' gap the author blamed on saturation.
A squared logit term does not help (0.521), so saturation in the logit is not the explanation for the misses.

The parts that check out: it is silent at D1 and GO, it fires only on a1->S1 D2 steps, and it grows with episode time and with the a1 logit. Base + time + choice reaches test 0.520. Misses show no large leftover error class beyond a small intercept offset (D1/GO +0.02, D2 a2 cells about -0.06 to -0.09). No future variables are used.
